summary: Transparent corporate forward-proxy returns 200 OK with body for CONNECT causing artifact/tunnel healthcheck mismatch and intermittent shard corruption
description:
Issue summary:
A customer on a private deployment is behind a corporate forward HTTP proxy that, for certain external hosts, responds to an HTTP CONNECT request with a normal 200/OK response line and a small HTML body (captive-portal style) instead of the canonical '200 Connection Established' or a 407. Redwood's artifact fetcher and the serving node healthcheck logic strictly expected the canonical CONNECT response and treated the reply as a protocol error, leading to partial tunnel establishment. Under load this manifested as intermittent TLS handshake failures over the created tunnel and partial/incorrect range responses when fetching large model shards, causing model-serving errors and shard verification failures.

Impact:
- Customer reported intermittent model-serving errors and failed requests for large generations lasting during heavy traffic windows (~10-20% of shard downloads failed with range/sha256 mismatch).
- Affected only private deployment behind corporate forward proxies implementing a captive-portal or misconfigured CONNECT response behavior.
- Control-plane auth succeeded; issue isolated to artifact download path when HTTPS_PROXY is present and proxy rewrites CONNECT replies.

Environment:
- Customer: Skyline Health, private deployment (VPC peered with Redwood control plane).
- Nodes affected: artifact fetcher (linux kernel 5.15, glibc 2.31), serving nodes doing shard range downloads.
- Regions: us-east-1.

Steps to reproduce (internal repro):
1. Stand up a simple forward HTTP proxy (squid/v2.7 compatible) and configure it to respond to CONNECT with: 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK' plus a small HTML body (simulate captive portal) rather than 'HTTP/1.1 200 Connection Established'.
2. Set HTTPS_PROXY to the proxy and attempt to download a large model shard from our presigned range URL via the artifact-downloader component.
3. Observe the CONNECT-response handler in the downloader logs and the resulting TLS handshake attempt over the tunnel.

Observed behavior:
- Artifact-downloader logs: 'CONNECT reply did not match expected token; found status="200 OK" body_length=345'.
- TLS handshake over the newly created tunnel sometimes fails with 'unexpected EOF' or 'tls: first record does not look like a TLS handshake'.
- When handshake fails mid-range, the server returns partial 206/Range responses causing SHA256 mismatch during shard verification.

Expected behavior:
- Proxy should respond with canonical '200 Connection Established' for CONNECT or return 407/401 to require authentication. Our downloader should accept a 200 with no body as success and then proceed with TLS handshake.

Logs & Attachments:
- Attached pcap and downloader debug logs (customer-provided).
- Example downloader log lines included in comments.

Notes on customer workaround applied:
- Customer temporarily bypassed the forward proxy for artifact hostnames via proxy bypass list for presigned S3 endpoints; this stopped shard errors immediately.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a forward HTTP proxy that replies to CONNECT with 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK' plus an HTML body (simulate captive portal). 2) Set HTTPS_PROXY to point at that proxy on a client node. 3) Use artifact-downloader to request a large presigned range URL. 4) Observe CONNECT parse path and TLS handshake failures in logs.
comments: Support (2026-03-12): Initial triage — customer reported 10% shard verification failures during nightly batch downloads. Confirmed issue only when node uses corporate forward proxy. Asked for pcap and verbose downloader logs.
Customer (2026-03-12): Uploaded pcap + proxy config. Notes that proxy appliance is an in-line security appliance that rewrites HTTP responses for blocked hosts (corporate captive portal).

SRE (2026-03-12): Reproduced locally with a squid instance configured to return '200 OK' and a small HTML body to CONNECT. Observed identical downloader behavior: parser rejects response and later TLS handshake failures.

ENG - artifact team (2026-03-13): Hypothesis: our CONNECT parser is too strict; it requires the substring 'Connection Established' rather than treating any 200 with no 'Proxy-Authenticate' and no response body as success. Also observed some implementations advertise HTTP/1.0 and include a body even on successful CONNECT — ambiguous behavior.

ENG (2026-03-14): Patch merged (runtime PR #4821) to: 1) accept status lines 'HTTP/1.0|1.1 200' as success if no 'Proxy-Authenticate' header and Content-Length / Transfer-Encoding indicate empty body; 2) if body exists, consume body and validate whether it's a captive portal (HTML) and fail fast; 3) add telemetry to surface CONNECT anomalies. Patch rolled to canary and then prod.

Customer (2026-03-14): Confirmed that after bypassing proxy for artifact hosts, shard failures stopped. After Redwood patch rollout, customer removed bypass and reports no further shard verification failures during 24h observation window.
investigation_notes: Parsed pcap shows proxy replying to CONNECT with 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK' and a small chunked HTML body. The downloader previously treated any non-exact '200 Connection Established' as a failure state and tore down the attempt or left the socket in indeterminate state.

curl and native glibc socket behavior are inconsistent across versions: some clients proceeded to TLS handshake despite non-canonical reason phrase; our downloader's stricter parser caused mismatch between perceived tunnel state and actual socket content.

Root cause: combination of (a) corporate forward proxy misconfiguration (returns a 200 with body for blocked hosts) and (b) conservative CONNECT response parsing in the artifact-downloader that didn't tolerate status-line variation and didn't robustly detect/handle response bodies prior to handing the socket to TLS layer.

Escalation to runtime team produced a small, low-risk change to be tolerant but conservative: accept 200 variants when safe, detect and fail fast on HTML bodies, and emit a detailed metric for any non-canonical CONNECT responses.
resolution: Patch deployed to artifact-downloader and serving node runtime (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821) on 2026-03-14 in canary and then all prod. The change makes CONNECT parsing tolerant to 'HTTP/1.0|1.1 200' reason-phrase variations when there is no body and no Proxy-Authenticate header, and fails fast if an HTML body is present (treats as captive portal).

Customer-side remediation: Skyline Health removed captive-portal/transparent rewrite for presigned artifact hostnames (added proxy-bypass entry) until patch was applied. After patch rollout, they restored normal proxy policy and observed no regressions.

Rollout notes: 2026-03-14 02:10 UTC canary (5 nodes), 2026-03-14 04:00 UTC full rollout. Metrics monitored: artifact-fetch success rate, shard-verify failures, CONNECT anomaly telemetry. All metrics returned to baseline within 30 minutes of full rollout.

Follow-ups: add a KB entry describing proxy recommendations for private deployments (avoid CONNECT reply bodies; use 407 for auth or canonical 200 Connection Established). Confluence page updated: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/proxy-connect-healthcheck-troubleshooting.
